openwrt_wiki.Einleitung: Raspberry Pi 4 has significantly higher spec CPU, RAM, and storage while maintaining the form factor, low power consumption, and passive cooling. Its capability can exceed many top tier routers. However it requires adding a USB 3.0 to gigabit ethernet adapter, gigabit switch, and wireless access point to reach similar networking functionality.
openwrt_wiki.Wireless Country Code: Setting the Country Code under Network -> Wireless in LuCI does not work with the Raspberry Pi, you will need to set the country code in the latest Raspberry Pi OS. Starting with Raspberry Pi 3 B+, the on-board WiFi won't even start if there is no country code.
openwrt_wiki.Updating the WiFi firmware: Only necessary prior to OpenWrt 21.02.3 (PR 9504). Older versions with the Pi 4B: trouble connecting to higher 5 GHz channels (channel 44 ok, 153 not); fixed by newer cypress firmware 7.45.234.
openwrt_wiki.Updating the EEPROM: bootloader EEPROM has many improvements since launch for performance, bug fixes, and power draw/thermal throttling issues; recommended to update; OpenWrt package bcm27xx-eeprom provides rpi-eeprom-*
openwrt_wiki.SoC-Tabelle BCM2711: BCM2711 | ARMv8 Cortex-A72 (Quad Core) | Videocore VI (@500MHz) | L2 1024KB
openwrt_wiki.Taktrate: The Pi 4 B originally shipped at 1.5GHz, later revisions include an improved onboard power supply and ship at 1.8GHz. Users should be sure to attach the self-adhesive heatsinks.
openwrt_wiki.Case Fan: official case fan and other GPIO fans: kmod-hwmon-gpiofan, dtoverlay=gpio-fan,gpiopin=14,temp=80000
openwrt_wiki.Power Notes: Often a 1A (2A for rpi4) is needed. If unsure, use the official Raspberry Pi 15W USB-C power supply (5.1V / 3.0A DC). Possible to supply power via GPIO pins. The early rpi4 model has an issue with some USB-C cables, this is fixed in rev 1.2 and newer. Thermal throttling was also improved, update the EEPROM.
openwrt_wiki.Serial: Serial is available via GPIO. Pin 6 Ground, Pin 8 TX, Pin 10 RX. Connect via RS232 at 3.3V (not older 12V). 115200 bps 8N1.

brcm2708: Add Raspberry Pi 4 support

- Support added to bcm2709 subtarget (32 bit).

Signed-off-by: Álvaro Fernández Rojas <noltari@gmail.com>

openwrt_image_mk.Device/rpi-4:
define Device/rpi-4
  DEVICE_MODEL := 4B/400/CM4/CM4S
  DEVICE_VARIANT := (64bit)
  KERNEL_IMG := kernel8.img
  DEVICE_DTS := \
	broadcom/bcm2711-rpi-4-b \
	broadcom/bcm2711-rpi-400 \
	broadcom/bcm2711-rpi-cm4-io \
	broadcom/bcm2711-rpi-cm4 \
	broadcom/bcm2711-rpi-cm4s
  SUPPORTED_DEVICES := \
	raspberrypi,400 \
	raspberrypi,4-compute-module \
	raspberrypi,4-compute-module-s \
	raspberrypi,4-model-b
  DEVICE_PACKAGES := \
	$(WIFI_43455_FW) \
	$(BRCM_WIFI_DRIVER) \
	$(LAN_DRIVERS)
  IMAGE/sysupgrade.img.gz := boot-common | boot-2711 | sdcard-img | gzip | append-metadata
  IMAGE/factory.img.gz := boot-common | boot-2711 | sdcard-img | gzip

gluon_targets_mk.zeile: $(eval $(call GluonTarget,bcm27xx,bcm2711)) # BROKEN: No 11s support, no reset button, sys LED issues

gluon_git.message:
bcm27xx-bcm2711: add (broken) support for the Raspberry Pi 4

Known issues:

* 11s is not working
* has no reset button, only SSH access, serial access or an external SD
  card update can return it to config mode at the moment
* LED: generally the red sys LED is working, including boot and failsafe
  blink patters, but:
  * sometimes not lit after boot
  * not blinking in config mode; instead sometimes either persistently on
    and sometimes persistently off after booting into config mode

Therefore adding it as broken.

However, due to its CPU power and small size still interesting as a VPN
offloader or WiFi rooftop core node (e.g. to Gluon'ify 5+60GHz devices).

Manifest aliases are added for upgrades from unreleased Gluon builds
and can be removed again at some point in the future.

Tested on a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B Rev 1.1.

Signed-off-by: Linus Lüssing <linus.luessing@c0d3.blue>
gluon_git.author: Linus Lüssing

rpi_doc_modelle.Zeichnungen: PDF RP-008343-DS, DXF RP-008342-DS, Schaltplan RP-008345-DS
rpi_doc_modelle.SoC: Broadcom BCM2711, 1.8 GHz quad-core 64-bit Arm Cortex-A72 (CPU) and 500 MHz VideoCore VI (GPU)
rpi_doc_modelle.Memory: LPDDR4 RAM that runs at 3200 MHz; a choice of 1, 2, 3, 4, or 8 GB of RAM
rpi_doc_modelle.Wireless module: dual-band (either 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz) 802.11ac Wi-Fi; Bluetooth 5.0 and BLE
rpi_doc_modelle.Ethernet PHY: dedicated PHY connects the Gigabit Ethernet interface in the SoC to the RJ45 port; Ethernet controller contained within the SoC; line speeds up to 1 Gb/s
rpi_doc_modelle.Gigabit Ethernet port: RJ45, two LEDs at the bottom (connectivity and activity); supports PoE when used with a PoE+ HAT
rpi_doc_modelle.PoE header: four-pin header located near the GPIO header; with PoE+ HAT draw power from Ethernet instead of USB-C
rpi_doc_modelle.AV jack: 3.5 mm, 4-pole stereo audio and composite video
rpi_doc_modelle.Micro-HDMI ports: HDMI0 and HDMI1, two 4K displays at 30 Hz or one 4K display at 60 Hz
rpi_doc_modelle.USB Type-C power port: 5 V at 3 A (15 W) required to power the board and attached peripherals
rpi_doc_modelle.Änderungen ggü. 3B+: USB-C statt Micro-USB, echtes Gigabit statt über USB-Controller, eigener USB-Controller, Bluetooth 5.0

rpi_doc_strom.Versorgung: All models require a 5.1V supply; Raspberry Pi 4 uses a USB-C connector; recommended 3A USB-C Supply for Raspberry Pi 4
rpi_doc_strom.PoE: The Ethernet jack on Raspberry Pi 4B and 3B+ is PoE capable, supporting the IEEE 802.3af-2003 PoE standard. All Raspberry Pi models with a PoE-capable Ethernet jack require a HAT to draw power through the Ethernet port.
rpi_doc_strom.Messbedingungen: Raspberry Pi OS June 2019, room temperature, HDMI monitor, USB keyboard and mouse, Pi 4 connected to Ethernet; without additional USB devices or HAT
rpi_doc_strom.PMIC: Extra PMIC features on Raspberry Pi 4 (Whitepaper RP-004340-WP)

rpi_doc_revision.Device-Tree: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B | raspberrypi | 4-model-b | brcm | bcm2711

rpi_doc_eeprom.BOOT_UART: On Raspberry Pi 4, the primary UART is exposed on GPIO 14 and 15. Configure the receiving debug terminal at 115200 bps, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, no parity.
rpi_doc_eeprom.SD-Überstrom: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, Raspberry Pi 5 ...: bootloader switches off power to the SD card on over-current
rpi_doc_eeprom.MAC: on Raspberry Pi 4 and 5 the MAC address is no longer generated from the serial number
rpi_doc_eeprom.Recovery: On a Raspberry Pi 4, the ROM can already load recovery.bin from the SD card
rpi_doc_eeprom.VL805: Raspberry Pi 4B USB configuration: two USB 3.0 ports and four USB 2.0 ports (VL805-Firmware)
rpi_doc_eeprom.POWER_OFF: On Raspberry Pi 4 version 1.3 and older, the configurable/long power off requires the XHCI controller to be enabled

rpi_datenblatt.Titel: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B Datasheet, Release 1.1, March 2024
rpi_datenblatt.Release History: 1 21/06/2019 First release; 1.1 12/03/2024 Updated obsolescence statement and electrical specification
rpi_datenblatt.Introduction: The Pi4B is available with 1, 2, 4, or 8 gigabytes of LPDDR4 SDRAM.
rpi_datenblatt.Hardware: Quad core 64-bit ARM-Cortex A72 running at 1.5GHz; 1, 2 and 4 Gigabyte LPDDR4 RAM options; H.265 4Kp60 decode; H.264 1080p60 decode; VideoCore VI; dual HDMI up to 4Kp60
rpi_datenblatt.Interfaces: 802.11 b/g/n/ac Wireless LAN; Bluetooth 5.0 with BLE; 1x SD Card; 2x micro-HDMI; 2x USB2; 2x USB3; 1x Gigabit Ethernet port (supports PoE with add-on PoE HAT); 1x CSI; 1x DSI; 28x user GPIO (up to 6x UART, 6x I2C, 5x SPI, SDIO, DPI, PCM, 2x PWM, 3x GPCLK)
rpi_datenblatt.DC Characteristics: VDD IO = 3.3V (GPIO bank tied to on-board 3.3V rail)
rpi_datenblatt.Power Requirements: good quality USB-C power supply capable of delivering 5V at 3A. If attached downstream USB devices consume less than 500mA, a 5V, 2.5A supply may be used.
rpi_datenblatt.GPIO: 28 BCM2711 GPIOs via standard 40-pin header; GPIO14 ALT0 TXD0, GPIO15 ALT0 RXD0
rpi_datenblatt.SD/SDIO: dedicated SD card socket, 1.8V DDR50 (50 MB/s peak)
rpi_datenblatt.USB: 2x USB2 and 2x USB3 type-A; downstream USB current limited to approximately 1.1A in aggregate
rpi_datenblatt.Temperature Range and Thermals: recommended ambient operating temperature range is 0 to 50 degrees Celsius; governor throttles so CPU never exceeds 85 degrees C; operates without extra cooling, for continuous load further cooling may be needed

rpi_produktbrief.Processor: Broadcom BCM2711, quad-core Cortex-A72 (Arm v8) 64-bit SoC @ 1.8GHz
rpi_produktbrief.Memory: 1GB, 2GB, 3GB, 4GB or 8GB LPDDR4 (depending on model) with on-die ECC
rpi_produktbrief.Connectivity: 2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz IEEE 802.11b/g/n/ac wireless LAN, Bluetooth 5.0, BLE; Gigabit Ethernet; 2 × USB 3.0 ports; 2 × USB 2.0 ports
rpi_produktbrief.Video and sound: 2 × micro HDMI ports (up to 4Kp60 supported); 2-lane MIPI DSI display port; 2-lane MIPI CSI camera port; 4-pole stereo audio and composite video port
rpi_produktbrief.Multimedia: H.265 (4Kp60 decode); H.264 (1080p60 decode, 1080p30 encode); OpenGL ES 3.0 graphics
rpi_produktbrief.SD card: microSD card slot for loading operating system and data storage
rpi_produktbrief.Input power: 5V DC via USB-C connector (minimum 3A); 5V DC via GPIO header (minimum 3A); Power over Ethernet (PoE)-enabled (requires separate PoE HAT); a good-quality 2.5A supply can be used if downstream USB peripherals consume less than 500mA in total
rpi_produktbrief.Overview: dual-band wireless LAN and Bluetooth have modular compliance certification; backwards compatible with Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+, similar power consumption
rpi_produktbrief.Safety warnings: external power supply rated at 5V/3A DC or 5.1V/3A DC minimum; well ventilated environment, case should not be covered; do not expose to water or moisture; designed for reliable operation at normal ambient room temperatures; PCB UL94-V0 (Compliance-Doku)
